items.details: Every stateful toolkit component implements ToData() *XxxData and LoadFromData(ctx, *XxxData, events.EventBus) (*Xxx, error). Data struct has JSON tags, no methods. Runtime struct has no JSON tags, holds event bus subscriptions. rpg-api serializes Data to Redis; calls LoadFromData before any rule call; calls ToData after to serialize the result back. Never (nil, nil) — always return a valid object or an error. Present in: character, Draft, BasicEnvironment, RoomData.

items.summary: ToJSON / LoadJSON for conditions and features (heterogeneous blobs)
items.details: When multiple runtime types share a single opaque JSON field (conditions list, features list), the pattern is: ToJSON() (json.RawMessage, error) for serialization; LoadJSON(json.RawMessage) (BehaviorType, error) for routing. LoadJSON peeks at ref.Value in the JSON, switches on it to the correct constructor, unmarshals the full struct. This keeps rpg-api's stored JSON opaque. Defined in rulebooks/dnd5e/conditions/loader.go and rulebooks/dnd5e/features/loader.go.

items.summary: BusEffect lifecycle: Apply subscribes, Remove unsubscribes, collect all errors on Remove
items.details: Any game mechanic that modifies behavior through events implements BusEffect: Apply(bus EventBus) error (subscribe handlers, store IDs), Remove(bus EventBus) error (unsubscribe all, clear IDs), IsApplied() bool. Remove must collect ALL unsubscribe errors (errors.Join or rpgerr accumulation) — never stop at the first failure. PR #603 established this convention. Stopping at first error leaves orphaned subscriptions.

items.summary: Refs package: typed constructors over raw strings
items.details: rulebooks/dnd5e/refs/ provides named ref constructors: refs.Features.Rage(), refs.Conditions.Dodging(), refs.CombatAbilities.Attack(), refs.Actions.Strike(). These are the canonical identifiers. Never use raw strings like 'rage' or 'dnd5e:features:rage' in switch cases or comparisons — always use refs.* or the module's typed constant. This makes identifiers greppable and refactorable.

items.summary: Testify suite pattern — mandatory for all non-example tests
items.details: All tests use suite.Suite + SetupTest() + s.Run() for subtests. SetupTest() creates fresh mocks and instances before each test function. SetupSubTest() resets shared test data before each s.Run(). Example tests (example_*_test.go) may be flat — they are documentation, not behavioral tests. Mocks go in mock/ subdirectory per module, generated with go:generate using uber's gomock.

items.summary: Input/Output types on every function — non-negotiable
items.details: Every function at every layer uses Input/Output struct types: func DoThing(ctx context.Context, input *DoThingInput) (*DoThingOutput, error). No positional parameters beyond ctx and input. This applies to internal helpers too. Never return (nil, nil) — always a valid object or an error. This is the workspace-wide rule enforced by CLAUDE.md.

items.summary: LayerOrchestrator FindPath is room-to-room, not intra-room
items.details: BasicRoomOrchestrator.FindPath(sourceRoomID, targetRoomID) returns a sequence of room IDs to traverse. It is not an A* within a single room. For intra-room pathfinding use SimplePathFinder.FindPath(start, goal CubeCoordinate, blocked) — but this is hex-only (issue #614). Square-grid intra-room pathfinding has no toolkit solution today.

items.summary: Encounter.NPCAct(npcID) wraps monster.TakeTurn, captures dnd5e-bus events via temporary subscription, re-emits as encounter-scoped per-viewer events
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.8 (rpg-toolkit#633). The Encounter aggregate exposes a single NPCAct verb that the rpg-api EndTurn handler calls when initiative advances to an NPC actor:

  func (e *Encounter) NPCAct(npcID core.EntityID) error

The verb's job:
  1. Build TurnInput from encounter state (active actor's snapshot, target list within perception, action economy budget).
  2. Subscribe a temporary listener to the dnd5e bus topics (AttackTopic, DamageTopic, ConditionTopic) for the duration of this NPC turn.
  3. Call monster.TakeTurn(turnInput) which decides + activates the NPC's chosen action.
  4. Capture every dnd5e bus event the NPC's action publishes during the call.
  5. Translate each captured event into an encounter-scoped per-viewer event (DamageDealtEvent, ConditionAppliedEvent) and publish through the encounter Broker. Viewer slicing happens here; consumers see what their PerceptionView allows.
  6. Unsubscribe the temporary listener (lifecycle scoped to the call).
  7. Internally call EndTurn to advance initiative; the next active actor (player or NPC) is the EndTurn handler's loop's responsibility (see pat-v2-npc-turn-dispatch on the api-member side).

Why temporary subscription (not durable): the dnd5e bus is process-wide; we don't want every encounter listening to every other encounter's events. Scope the subscription to the NPCAct call only.

Validated reality note (2026-05-09): the dnd5e action layer (bite, scimitar, melee, ranged) currently only publishes the cause AttackEvent without resolution data. The encounter SDK uses a STAND-IN RESOLVER inside NPCAct: d20 + AttackBonus vs target AC, damage rolled from DamageDice, nat-20 crit, nat-1 miss; uses MonsterData snapshot fields. The captured-damage / captured-condition listener paths are wired but currently no-op until rpg-toolkit#635 lands. Once #635 ships, drop the stand-in resolver and rely on the captured paths.

items.summary: Combat events follow the per-viewer + sealed-type pattern as DoorOpenedEvent. AttackResolved is cause; DamageDealt + ConditionApplied are effects
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.8 (rpg-toolkit#633). Combat events live in encounter/events/ and follow the existing sealed-type + per-viewer-projection pattern established by DoorOpenedEvent / HexRevealedEvent / EntityAppearedEvent in Wave 2.7 (see encounter/events/door_opened.go as the template). New events:

  - AttackResolvedEvent — cause-stage. Carries attacker, target, action ref, hit/miss/critical, attack roll, total. Publishes once per attack resolution.
  - DamageDealtEvent — effect-stage. Carries target, amount, hp_after.{current,max}, damage type, source attacker. Publishes once per damage application.
  - ConditionAppliedEvent — effect-stage. Carries target, condition ref, source ref, duration. Publishes once per condition application.
  - TurnStartedEvent / TurnEndedEvent — initiative lifecycle. Carry the actor id + round.
  - ModeChangedEvent — mode flip (FREE_ROAM ↔ TURN_BASED). Carries new mode.

Every event implements the sealed events.EncounterEvent interface and carries a PerPlayer map: each viewer's PlayerID → that viewer's slice of the event (or absence). The Broker delivers based on PerPlayer; the rpg-api translator handles per-viewer slicing on the wire (see api-member's pat-v2-combat-event-translator).

Cause vs effect split (validated in Wave 2.7, reused in 2.8): cause and effect are SEPARATE events with INDEPENDENT per-viewer projections. Two viewers might see different halves (stealth, line-of-sight). Don't merge them inside the toolkit, even if 'they always fire together' for the simple case — different waves will introduce viewers who see one but not the other.

Validated reality note (2026-05-09): AttackResolvedEvent is implemented and ready but doesn't fire from the dnd5e action layer today (see pat-encounter-npc-verb stand-in note). Once rpg-toolkit#635 wires combat.ResolveAttack into bite/scimitar/melee/ranged, AttackResolvedEvent will start flowing through the NPC capture path.

When adding a new combat event (HealReceived, ConditionRemoved, Knockback): copy door_opened.go's shape, define the per-viewer slice, document whether it's cause-stage or effect-stage, and add a translator case in rpg-api's translate_combat.go.

items.summary: Mode + initiative + active-actor live on encounter.Data. SetMode rolls initiative on flip; EndTurn advances ActiveIdx; round increments on wrap
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.8 (rpg-toolkit#633). encounter.Data grew Wave-2.8 fields:

  type Data struct {
      // ... existing Wave 2.5/2.6/2.7 fields ...
      Mode        core.EncounterMode  // Unspecified | FreeRoam | TurnBased
      Initiative  []core.EntityID     // ordered list of actor ids; both players + monsters
      ActiveIdx   int                 // index into Initiative; wraps to 0 on round end
      Round       int                 // 1-indexed; increments when ActiveIdx wraps
      Monsters    map[EntityID]*MonsterData  // NPC actors with MonsterRef + AC + HP + AttackBonus + DamageDice + Position + ...
  }

Verbs that mutate this state:
  - SetMode(newMode) — flip between FreeRoam and TurnBased. On a flip TO TurnBased, rolls initiative for every actor (players + monsters) and populates Initiative. On a flip TO FreeRoam, clears Initiative + ActiveIdx + Round (or preserves for retry — design choice, currently clears).
  - EndTurn(actorID) — validates actorID matches the current ActiveActor, advances ActiveIdx; if ActiveIdx wraps past len(Initiative)-1, resets to 0 and increments Round. Publishes TurnEndedEvent for the leaving actor + TurnStartedEvent for the new active actor.
  - NPCAct(npcID) — see pat-encounter-npc-verb. Internally calls EndTurn after the NPC's action.

Queries:
  - Mode() core.EncounterMode
  - InitiativeOrder() []core.EntityID (defensive copy)
  - ActiveActor() core.EntityID — returns Initiative[ActiveIdx] or empty if out of range.
  - Round() int

Persistence: ToData() and LoadFromData() round-trip all five new fields. Mode is serialized as int (its enum representation). MonsterData uses the same JSON shape as PlayerData — see pat-001 (ToData / LoadFromData persistence pattern) for the convention.

When extending: new turn-related state (action economy on the active actor's turn, reaction window state, delay/ready actions) lives on encounter.Data alongside these fields. New verbs that mutate turn state go on the Encounter aggregate, not on Monster or Player — keep one source of truth for the initiative cycle.

items.summary: encounter.Data.PendingPrompts map[PlayerID]*PendingPrompt is single source of truth for caller-private prompt state; SubmitCheck verb is the resolution path; at-most-one-pending invariant enforced by ErrPromptAlreadyPending
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.9 (rpg-toolkit PR #641). encounter.Data grew Wave-2.9 fields:

  type Data struct {
      // ... existing Wave 2.5-2.8 fields ...
      PendingPrompts map[core.PlayerID]*PendingPrompt
  }

  type PendingPrompt struct {
      Kind            PromptKind   // SkillCheck | Dialogue | TargetSelect (Wave 2.9 implements SkillCheck only)
      DC              int
      Ability         string       // "DEX", "STR", ... — 5e short codes
      Tool            *core.Ref    // optional tool proficiency check (e.g. dnd5e:item:thieves-tools)
      TriggeredBy     core.EntityID  // the door/trap/NPC that issued the prompt
      TriggeredAction string       // what to do on success (Wave 2.9: "open")
  }

Verbs that mutate prompt state:
  - AttemptUnlock(playerID, doorID) — called from rpg-api's Interact handler when target is a locked door. Validates: door exists, door is Locked, no prompt already pending for this player. If a prompt is already pending → ErrPromptAlreadyPending (FailedPrecondition on the wire). On success, populates PendingPrompts[playerID] from DoorData (LockDC / LockAbility / LockTool fields → PendingPrompt). Returns nil; the rpg-api handler reads data.PendingPrompts[playerID] back out for the wire response.
  - SubmitCheck(playerID, roll) — clears the prompt regardless of outcome (success, failure, even unsupported-action error). On success, dispatches the prompt's TriggeredAction against TriggeredBy (Wave 2.9: only "open" wired → calls OpenDoor internally). Returns SubmitCheckResult{Success bool, Total int}.

At-most-one-pending invariant: enforced inside AttemptUnlock (and any future prompt-issuing verb). Single-slot per player, fail-fast on collision. No queueing.

Why on the toolkit not rpg-api: prompts ARE encounter-scoped game state — DC, ability, tool selection are rule decisions, and dispatch on success is rule logic. Per pat-009 (web-side, but mirrors here): rules in toolkit. rpg-api's job is wire shape + persistence + auth.

When adding a new prompt-issuing verb (BeginDialogue from NPC, TriggerTrap on stepping): same shape — verb sets PendingPrompts[playerID] from the source's data fields, returns nil; rpg-api handler reads it back and ships the wire response. SubmitCheck remains the single resolution path; extend dispatchPromptAction with the new TriggeredAction value.

items.summary: DoorData carries Locked + LockDC + LockAbility + LockTool; AttemptUnlock issues a pending prompt; SubmitCheck-success calls OpenDoor internally and emits DoorOpenedEvent per viewer
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.9 (rpg-toolkit PR #641). DoorData grew lock-state fields:

  type DoorData struct {
      // ... existing Wave 2.7 fields (ID, Position, Open, etc.) ...
      Locked       bool
      LockDC       int        // skill check DC required to unlock
      LockAbility  string     // 5e ability short code, typically "DEX"
      LockTool     *core.Ref  // optional tool proficiency, typically dnd5e:item:thieves-tools
  }

Flow on the rpg-api side (mirrors pat-v2-interact-handler-shape):
  1. Interact handler resolves target_entity_id to a DoorData.
  2. If door.Locked == true: handler calls enc.AttemptUnlock(playerID, doorID) instead of enc.OpenDoor.
  3. AttemptUnlock populates encounter.Data.PendingPrompts[playerID] from door.LockDC/LockAbility/LockTool with TriggeredAction="open".
  4. Handler reads PendingPrompts[playerID] back out, builds InputRequired{skill_check}, sets it on InteractResponse.input_required.
  5. NO stream events emitted for the prompt itself — caller-private. (Mirrors api-side pat-v2-prompt-on-response.)
  6. Player submits a roll via SubmitCheck. On success, the toolkit's dispatchPromptAction ("open" branch) calls OpenDoor internally — which fires DoorOpenedEvent + HexRevealedEvent per viewer through the Broker, same path as Wave 2.7's unlocked-door flow.
  7. On failure, prompt is cleared and the door stays locked; no events emit. Future waves may add a CheckFailedEvent for trap-trigger-on-fail consequences.

If door.Locked == false: behavior is unchanged from Wave 2.7 — handler calls enc.OpenDoor directly, no prompt machinery.

When adding a new lock-shape (key items, magical wards, password-prompt doors): extend DoorData with the additional fields, add a new prompt Kind if the resolution shape differs from skill_check (e.g. ItemCheck for keys), extend dispatchPromptAction with the success-branch dispatch. Wave 2.9's structure makes this additive — DoorData and PendingPrompt grow new fields rather than spawning parallel types.

items.summary: WithCharacterResolver(...) is the toolkit-owned interface for character-state lookups (ability scores, tool proficiencies); rpg-api wires the implementation, toolkit owns the math
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.9 (rpg-toolkit PR #641). The encounter SDK exposes a CharacterResolver interface and a WithCharacterResolver(resolver) functional option for tkenc.New / LoadFromData:

  type CharacterResolver interface {
      AbilityModifier(playerID core.PlayerID, ability string) (int, error)
      ToolProficiencyBonus(playerID core.PlayerID, tool *core.Ref) (int, error)
  }

  func WithCharacterResolver(r CharacterResolver) Option

The encounter aggregate holds the resolver internally; SubmitCheck (and any future modifier-needing verb) calls through the interface to compute totals: total = roll + resolver.AbilityModifier(playerID, prompt.Ability) + resolver.ToolProficiencyBonus(playerID, prompt.Tool).

If no resolver is wired and SubmitCheck is called → ErrNoCharacterResolver. This is a load-time configuration error, not a runtime / data error — the rpg-api side mirrors with pat-v2-thread-resolver-everywhere (every LoadFromData / tkenc.New call site must thread the option).

Stability: the interface contract is intended to be stable. Only the implementation will change as the character store integration improves (rpg-api#516 tracks the rpg-api side's character-resolver maturation — currently a thin shim around character.Data lookups; future versions may add caching, batched lookups, equipment-aware modifiers).

When adding a new modifier-needing verb (saving throws, attack rolls if combat resolver migrates here, contested checks): extend CharacterResolver with the new method, add the verb's modifier-pulling logic. Keep the interface focused on character-state lookups; world-state lookups (terrain, line-of-sight) belong on different abstractions (PerceptionView, etc.).

items.summary: Reality note: SubmitCheck clears the pending prompt regardless of outcome; capture triggeredBy/triggeredAction BEFORE the delete so a downstream OpenDoor failure doesn't strand stale prompt state
items.details:
Implementation reality discovered while building Wave 2.9 (rpg-toolkit PR #641). The SubmitCheck verb clears `encounter.Data.PendingPrompts[playerID]` regardless of outcome:
  - Success → clear, then dispatch TriggeredAction (e.g., OpenDoor).
  - Failure → clear, emit nothing.
  - Unsupported-action error (TriggeredAction not in dispatchPromptAction's known set) → clear, return ErrUnsupportedPromptAction.

Why clear-on-all-outcomes: leaving a stale prompt around after a failed roll would let the player retry indefinitely without burning an action — they could just keep submitting rolls until they succeeded. The intentional cost of failure is "lose the prompt; need to Interact again to retry." If a future wave wants a different cost model (e.g., advantage on retry within N seconds), make that an explicit verb option, not a side effect of leaving the prompt set.

Implementation gotcha: capture `triggeredBy` and `triggeredAction` into local variables BEFORE deleting `PendingPrompts[playerID]`. The naive ordering — delete first, then dispatch — would lose the dispatch info. The correct ordering caught in PR #641's implementation:

  prompt := data.PendingPrompts[playerID]
  triggeredBy := prompt.TriggeredBy
  triggeredAction := prompt.TriggeredAction
  delete(data.PendingPrompts, playerID)

  if !success { return SubmitCheckResult{Success: false, Total: total}, nil }
  return e.dispatchPromptAction(playerID, triggeredBy, triggeredAction, total)

A downstream OpenDoor failure (e.g., door doesn't exist anymore because another player opened it concurrently) thus returns the error without leaving a stale prompt for the player to retry against a missing target. The prompt is gone; the player must re-Interact to get a fresh prompt against current world state.

items.summary: Reality note: dispatchPromptAction only wires "open" in Wave 2.9; other TriggeredAction values return ErrUnsupportedPromptAction; future waves extend the dispatch table
items.details:
Implementation reality from Wave 2.9 (rpg-toolkit PR #641). The dispatchPromptAction internal helper is a small switch on TriggeredAction:

  func (e *Encounter) dispatchPromptAction(playerID core.PlayerID, triggeredBy core.EntityID, triggeredAction string, total int) (SubmitCheckResult, error) {
      switch triggeredAction {
      case "open":
          return e.openDoorFromPrompt(playerID, triggeredBy, total)
      default:
          return SubmitCheckResult{}, ErrUnsupportedPromptAction
      }
  }

Wave 2.9 ships only the "open" branch — locked-door unlock dispatching to internal OpenDoor. Other TriggeredAction values that future waves will add:
  - "disarm" — successful trap disarm prompt → toolkit verb that flips trap.Disarmed = true.
  - "persuade", "intimidate", "deceive" — NPC dialogue branch outcomes; dispatch may not need a world-state mutation (the dialogue tree advances via separate verb).
  - "force-open", "break" — STR-check alternative on the same lock; dispatches to OpenDoor with a damage side-effect.

When adding a new TriggeredAction:
  1. Add the case to dispatchPromptAction.
  2. Implement the action helper as a private method on Encounter (e.g., disarmTrapFromPrompt). Keep it private — public verbs route through SubmitCheck, not directly to dispatch.
  3. Document the action string in PendingPrompt's docstring (it's the contract between AttemptUnlock-style verbs and dispatch).
  4. Test via the SubmitCheck integration path, not a direct dispatch call.

Do NOT make TriggeredAction a typed enum yet — the set is small and string-shaped works for the current waves. Tighten when the set grows past ~6 actions or when external callers need to introspect.
